guidance: A printed vertical line between columns (a column rule) counts as a gap. The line may run along the rule.
If there is print on only one side of the line, or on neither side (blank paper, the foot of a page), pick Yes as long as the line crosses no print. The dark edge of the scan is not print.
An advertisement, a picture or a heading across several columns counts as print. If the line goes through one, pick No.
If the line runs between two pictures or two cartoon panels, pick Yes.
If the line is mostly in a gap but crosses a few letters, pick No.
intro: Each crop comes from an English-language page in Chronicling America. A program drew a line on it where it thinks two columns of text are separated.
name: English column gutters
question: Does this line run down a gap between columns of text without crossing any printed text?
rules: Pick Yes if the line runs down the gap between two columns and crosses no print. Use Hide the line (L) to see the print under it. You don't need to read the text, only see where the print is.
title: English newspaper column gutters
